A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Composer study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite reformatting and relocation of material.

before.justification: v1 reports original architecture-search experiments, model pretraining, downstream evaluations, efficiency measurements, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds downstream evaluation results for 8B models in Table 6.

M1.justification: The search procedures, MAD evaluator, Nc aggregation, and stacking/stretching mechanisms remain unchanged. The added Bayesian-optimization specifications document implementation details; the 8B architectures apply the existing extrapolation procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use DCLM, MAD, BabiStories, and the same six downstream tasks: ARC-Challenge, ARC-Easy, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, SciQ, and PIQA. Adding 8B models changes model configurations, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The Llama 3.2, Sandwich Transformer, three Striped Attention variants, STAR, and random-architecture comparisons remain. v2 corrects the appendix descriptions of the 1:4 and 1:8 Striped blocks to match their existing Section 4.3 definitions; this does not establish a change to the comparators actually evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 extends the evaluated model sizes from 350M, 1B, and 3B to include 8B, with downstream results reported under the existing 4e20-FLOP evaluation description. Existing training budgets and inference procedures are retained. Table 2's new metric clarification does not establish that the earlier evaluation procedure changed.

E4.justification: The search-method, dataset, width/depth, extrapolation, and aggregation ablations are retained, along with random-architecture comparisons, ranking correlations, and scaling and efficiency analyses. The expanded aggregation rationale adds explanation without a new empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed variation, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain the same inference averaging procedure using three warm-up prompts and five measured prompts. The new Monte Carlo interpretation of aggregation does not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises ARC-Easy scores and averages for Llama, Sandwich, and all three Striped baselines; for example, Llama changes from 56.8 to 61.03 on ARC-Easy and from 58.0 to 58.69 overall. Composite and STAR rows are unchanged. Table 6 corrects the 3B stretched average from 66.9 to 62.0 and adds 8B averages of 69.3, 69.7, and 70.4 for Llama, stacked, and stretched models. Existing result plots remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix D.5 newly relates N0 selection to maximizing a product of marginal frequencies under layerwise independence and asserts statistical consistency under this marginal model. This adds a limited theoretical assertion without a proof. The existing search-space definitions and Equations 1-11 remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract extends the claimed evaluation scale from 350M-3B to 350M-8B and replaces the earlier improvement range with 2-2.1% average accuracy improvement. The introduction reduces its stated loss advantage to 0.03. Key Result 3 explicitly qualifies the comparison by fixed training tokens and lowers its maximum accuracy-improvement claim from 4.35-4.9% to 3.7%. The central contribution remains unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds the interpretation that Bayesian search already captures inter-layer dependencies, allowing N0 aggregation to ignore explicit conditioning while preserving useful patterns. It also adds a signal/gradient-propagation explanation for stretching. The long-context and reasoning limitations already appeared in v1 Appendix A and are retained in v2 Section 5.

D1.justification: v2 specifies BoTorch SingleTaskGP, an RBF kernel, dimension-scaled priors, and qLogNEI. It adds raw-versus-normalized accuracy information to Table 2, supplies 8B layer sequences, and corrects the Striped Attention appendix descriptions. However, the model-dimension and training-setting tables still stop at 3B.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against traditional NAS, Nemotron/PostNAS, and STAR are retained. Reference changes concern formatting and bibliographic details rather than added research or revised relationships to prior work.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative are preserved. v2 moves the appendix discussion into Section 5, renumbers subsequent material, adds acknowledgments, revises front matter, and adds localized implementation and aggregation explanations.

P2.justification: The document undergoes extensive reformatting into the ICLR template, changing the title/abstract presentation, typography, margins, running headers, and figure/table placement throughout. The extrapolation illustration moves from v1 Figure 16 in the appendix to v2 Figure 2 in the main text. Table 6 gains an 8B block, while the original figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting the 3B average, clarifying Table 2 metrics, and moderating performance claims improve reporting accuracy. Added 8B results and Bayesian-optimization details provide limited gains in evidence and reproducibility. These benefits remain modest: 8B settings are incompletely tabulated, the retained claim of improvement on all downstream tasks has exceptions, and the new aggregation-consistency assertion is unproved.
